question: Should Plite allow ordinary accepted edits without an author ID when the authored capability is installed?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; redesign-from-first-principles; Best API hard-cut; Plate Plan and Plite Plan ownership
trigger: A generic registry editor threw on its first ordinary edit because SuggestionKit installs native authored changes and the editor had no current user ID. The user requested a fresh Best API Review of why identity is required.
requirements: Preserve one causal mutation model for accepted and proposed content, including dependencies, rebasing, collaboration admission and atomic review decisions.
Preserve retained accepted history and selective compensation without inventing or corrupting author attribution.
Allow actorless reading and rendering of an authored document while rejecting any write that would create unattributed authored facts.
Keep authentication policy in the application; Plite may require a non-empty author ID but cannot claim that it authenticated the identity.
Keep ordinary editors free of the authored requirement unless their selected composition installs the authored capability.
evidenceReuse: Reaffirms the accepted native authored owner and direct-checkpoint model from 2026-09-13. This review rechecked current AuthoredOptions, transaction capture, accepted-history behavior, Plate's runtime user bridge, SuggestionPlugin dependency and the generic registry composition. It did not repeat the checkpoint benchmark or the broader suggestion audit.
summary: Stop making author identity optional for accepted edits through the authored engine. Every non-empty document write is emitted as one authored edit operation; proposal=false changes still carry causal identity, rebase pending work and support retained selective history. Plite already permits actorless reads by accepting a resolver that returns null and validates identity only when a write starts. The registry failure was composition wiring, and the current demo supplies userId: 'demo'. The runtime wording is inaccurate: a non-empty author ID is required, while authentication remains application policy.
alternatives: Chosen target: keep one authored operation path for accepted and proposed writes; require a current author ID for either path, while allowing read-only authored views without one.
Validate identity only in proposing mode: rejected because accepted edits are proposal=false authored operations that rebase pending work and participate in retained history and compensation.
Generate an anonymous or system author inside Plite: rejected because it fabricates domain attribution, weakens same-author rules and makes persistence depend on an implicit identity lifecycle.
Bypass authored capture for accepted edits: rejected because it creates two mutation authorities and removes causal facts needed by pending changes, collaboration and selective reversal.

Require identity when the editor is constructed or the plugin activates: rejected because actorless read-only rendering and identity that becomes available later are valid; the first authored write is the truthful validation boundary.

Remove SuggestionKit from every generic composition: rejected as an engine redesign; app-owned kits may omit the capability, while a demo that intentionally includes it may supply a stable demo identity.
proofLimits: Current-source inspection and focused tests establish the local identity boundary: the unattributed proposed write rejects, accepted native typing remains in authored history, and registry suggestion behavior passes. The earlier exact runtime reproduction also showed editing intent rejects without userId and succeeds with one. This review does not replay collaboration, persistence, browser or scale suites, and it does not certify the misleading error text as repaired.
